title: 1 Samuel 2:18–21
context: A brief contrast: the child Samuel ministers before the LORD, Hannah brings him a robe each year, Eli blesses the family, and the LORD gives Hannah more children.

verses.text: But Samuel ministered before the LORD, being a child, clothed with a linen ephod.
verses.arminianNotes: “But Samuel ministered before the LORD, being a child, clothed with a linen ephod.” Arminian readers see faithful service from a child set against the corruption of grown priests.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see God preparing his servant in the midst of a failing priesthood. The linen ephod marks Samuel’s role in sanctuary service from an early age.

verses.text: Moreover his mother made him a little robe, and brought it to him from year to year when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.
verses.arminianNotes: Hannah brings Samuel a little robe each year when she comes to sacrifice. Arminian readers see a mother’s continued love and faithfulness after giving her son to God.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see Hannah’s devotion continuing year by year. The tender detail shows that dedicating Samuel did not end her care for him.

verses.text: Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, and said, “May the LORD give you offspring from this woman for the petition which was asked of the LORD.” Then they went to their own home.
verses.arminianNotes: Eli blesses the couple: “May the LORD give you offspring from this woman for the petition which was asked of the LORD.” Arminian readers see a priestly blessing that honors Hannah’s faithfulness.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see God’s further generosity anticipated. “Seed” is an alternative rendering for “offspring”; that is a translation note, not a textual variant.

verses.text: The LORD visited Hannah, and she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters. The child Samuel grew before the LORD.
verses.arminianNotes: The LORD visits Hannah, and she bears three sons and two daughters, while the narrator adds, “The child Samuel grew before the LORD.” Arminian readers see God’s abundant kindness after her costly gift.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see God’s generous blessing beyond what Hannah asked. The repeated note on Samuel’s growth keeps him at the center of God’s plan.
